plan_title: Elk Hills A1-A2 and 26R CO2 Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan
ama_definition: The modeled plume area at t = three years after injection ends (30 years after start) plus a half-mile buffer; one AMA held for 30 years and treated as functionally equivalent to the MMA (p18, p21).
mma_definition: The modeled extent of the CO2 plume at 100 years post-injection plus a half-mile buffer, shown as the blue line in Figure 8 (p18, p20).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only existing wellbores and pipelines/surface equipment are treated as realistic (low likelihood; wellbore leakage magnitude bounded at under 1% of injection). Faults, seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, future drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated negligible or not anticipated (p24-31).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection baselines: fluid chemistry and pressure/temperature at each monitoring well collected during construction (quarterly sampling and continuous P/T at above-confining-zone wells; one-time chemistry plus continuous P/T in the injection zone), and at least 12 months of seismic network data before first injection. Operational data (injection set-points, inspections, personal monitor alarms) also serve as a working baseline for flagging excursions (p38-40).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report (filed March 31 with other GHG reports) with mass balance and estimated leakage; records kept at least three years. Table 4 notes parallel reporting of well incidents to CalGEM or EPA UIC and of surface leaks under Subpart W; monitoring well procedures follow the Class VI permit. No commitment to publish measurement data (p32, p39-40, p43-44).

rows.detail: Custody-transfer meters at each CO2 source measure mass flow continuously with composition continuous or by periodic sampling; operations/composition meter at the recompression facility outlet; meters calibrated every 60-90 days; continuous stream analysis.
rows.location: CO2 source off-take points and recompression facility outlet
rows.evidence_quote: The custody-transfer meters will measure flow rate continuously.

rows.detail: Injection pressure, temperature and rate monitored continuously through SCADA at the Central Control Facility, staffed 24 hours; high/low set-points per injector flag excursions, which are screened for leakage.
rows.trigger_or_response: Readings outside set-points: automatic flag, field personnel investigate; unresolved issues get detailed investigation and a work order; leaks quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: Injection well pressure, temperature, and injection rate will be monitored continuously.

rows.detail: Changes in annulus pressure monitored to detect tubing leaks; annular leakage detection devices are part of the corrosion/integrity program.
rows.trigger_or_response: Tubing leak indicated: workover crews respond within days.
rows.evidence_quote: Monitor changes in annulus pressure; MIT for injectors

rows.detail: Internal and external MITs (Table 5 says annual), including radioactive tracer surveys and standard annular pressure tests; SAPT initially and whenever the packer is replaced or reset; MIT before injection, after workovers, and per UIC schedule.
rows.trigger_or_response: Failed MIT: shut in immediately, notify CalGEM/EPA; repair and retest within 180 days or plug and abandon.
rows.evidence_quote: All active injection wells undergo MIT before

rows.detail: Dedicated plume monitoring wells in the sequestration reservoir with continuous pressure and temperature gauges, fluid composition sampling and periodic cased-hole logs; three wells for 26R, two for A1-A2.
rows.trigger_or_response: Deviation from baseline assessed for indications of leakage.
rows.evidence_quote: Dedicated wells monitoring sequestration reservoir with pressure, temperature, fluid composition, and periodic cased hole logs

rows.detail: Routine field inspections by about 40 trained personnel looking for white CO2 clouds, ice and fluid leaks at wells, pipelines and facilities; manned surface facilities visited daily.
rows.location: Field-wide wells, pipelines and surface facilities
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak seen: investigate, work order, quantify for the annual report; workover crews respond within days.
rows.evidence_quote: Field personnel visit manned surface facilities daily to conduct visual inspection.

rows.detail: ToxiRAE Pro CO2 monitors (0-50,000 ppm, 100 ppm resolution) worn by all field personnel, alarm at 1,000 ppm or lower; used as a supplement for small leaks missed visually.
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, verify monitor, investigate source; confirmed leak quantified and reported.
rows.evidence_quote: CO2 gas monitors will be worn by all field personnel (ToxiRAE Pro CO2 or equivalent;

rows.detail: Targeted soil gas flux monitoring only after a surface leak or damaging seismic event is detected, used to quantify the leak.
rows.trigger_or_response: Detected leakage or Mw>2.0 event with confirmed damage: targeted survey; leak quantified from flow rate and concentration.
rows.evidence_quote: Targeted surface air and/or soil gas flux monitoring will be conducted in the event of detected leakage

rows.detail: One USDW monitoring well per project in the Tulare Formation (400-450 ft for 26R, 940-960 ft for A1-A2): quarterly fluid sampling for cations, anions, dissolved CO2, methane, isotopes, plus continuous pressure and temperature.
rows.location: USDW monitoring wells, one per project area
rows.trigger_or_response: Deviation from baseline assessed; increased CO2 in groundwater mapped as isoconcentrations to quantify leakage.
rows.evidence_quote: These dedicated wells will monitor the sequestration reservoir, zones above the sequestration reservoir, and the USDW.

rows.detail: Above-zone wells 355X-26R and 327-7R-RD1 in the Etchegoin Formation with continuous pressure/temperature and quarterly fluid sampling; distributed temperature sensing fiber at Etchegoin and Tulare depths in plume wells.
rows.location: Etchegoin Formation above the Reef Ridge shale, both project areas
rows.trigger_or_response: Anomaly indicating fault or wellbore leakage: shut in injectors near faults; re-enter and reseal abandoned wells.
rows.evidence_quote: Monitoring wells with pressure, temperature, fluid composition, and periodic cased-hole logs

rows.detail: Periodic cased-hole logs in monitoring wells; cement bond logs and radioactive tracer surveys listed as part of the corrosion and mechanical integrity program; log types and interval not specified.

Dedicated seven-station network of surface and borehole (>1,500 ft) three-component geophones detecting events down to Mw 0.0, continuous with near-real-time telemetry; also watches Southern California Seismic Network stations 5-8 miles away.
rows.trigger_or_response: Event above Mw 2.0 with confirmed local damage: investigate for leakage; shut in injectors near the event.
rows.evidence_quote: Seven sensor locations (borehole and near surface) with high-sensitivity 3-component geophones.

rows.detail: Existing 3D seismic survey, reprocessed in 2019, used for characterization and fault mapping; VSPs cited only for the seismic network velocity model. No repeat seismic committed.
rows.evidence_quote: While developing the EHOF, a seismic survey was conducted to characterize the formations

rows.detail: Targeted point-source surface air monitoring near a leaking wellbore or other detected leak, used to quantify the leak from flow rate and CO2 concentration.
rows.trigger_or_response: Detected wellbore or surface leak: targeted air monitoring; mass quantified for the annual report.
rows.evidence_quote: Targeted point-source surface air monitoring will be conducted in the event of detected wellbore leakage

rows.detail: Subpart W emission factors and engineering estimates for equipment leaks and vents between the injection meter and wellhead; reconciled with event-driven quantification to avoid double counting.
rows.evidence_quote: 40 CFR 98.230-238 (Subpart W) is used to estimate surface leaks from equipment at the EHOF.

rows.detail: Corrosion monitoring with coupons and casing integrity checks on well materials, pipelines and surface equipment; corrosion-resistant materials specified for CO2 service.
rows.location: Well materials, pipelines and other surface equipment

rows.detail: Geophysical monitoring 'as approved in the Class VI permit' to track plume extent against lateral migration; method, instruments and frequency not described in this plan.
rows.evidence_quote: Geophysical monitoring conducted as approved in the Class VI permit will track the extent of CO2 plume

rows.detail: Process instrumentation on pipelines and facilities feeding the 24/7 Central Control Facility to spot leaks, with manual and automatic shutdowns; remote monitoring of pumps and valves.
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak indication: manual or automatic shutdown; workover crews respond within days.
rows.evidence_quote: Instrumentation will be installed on pipelines and facilities that allows the 24/7 operations staff at the Central Control Facility (CCF) to monitor the process

notes: Figure and equation pages (7-12, 14, 16, 19, 20, 22, 23, 27, 29, 31, 35 and the equations in Section 7) are largely image-only. production_monitoring is not_found because the plan states no CO2 will be produced or recycled (p34); Table 4 does list 'anomalous pressure or gas composition from productive shallower zones' as a detector for abandoned-well leakage, presumably from existing Etchegoin production, but no program is described (p32). MIT frequency conflicts: Table 5 says annual (p34) while Section 4.2 says before injection, after workovers or per UIC schedule (p24-25); annual used. Above-zone and groundwater quarterly sampling frequencies come from Appendix 11.6 tables for the injection phase; Section 6.3 describes the same quarterly/continuous scheme for the baseline period. Well list names plume well 374-36R but the monitoring table names 376-36R (p51-52). Geophysical plume monitoring (p31) is a bare commitment deferred to the Class VI permit, so it is coded under other rather than active_seismic. The seismic network's 'near real-time' telemetry and Mw 0.0 detection threshold are design specifications; response actions are deferred to the Class VI permit except the Mw 2.0 damage trigger (p38). Plan implementation anticipated Q1 2025 or 90 days after EPA approval (p43).
